utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Can we have the appearances, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Turone and I am appear with my colleague, Ms. McHenry and with the case manager Mr. Huber for the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we have the appearances for the Defence, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Judge, we seem to be having a problem with the court reporter hearing something.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can it be heard now? Can the English booth be heard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm Tomislav Kuzmanovic along with my colleague, our legal assistant, Niko Duric are here for Zlavko Mucic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, because I see no text after my name, may I repeat? I'm Edina Residovic, Defence counsel -- shall I repeat it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You can repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic appearing on behalf of Mr. Zejnil Delalic along with my colleague Professor Eugene O'Sullivan from Canada. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I'm Salih Karabdic attorney from Sarajevo appearing on behalf of Mr. Hazim Delic along with Thomas Moran, attorney from Houston, Texas.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I'm Cynthia McMurrey appearing for Mr. Esad Landzo along with Ms. Nancy Boler. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: May we have the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly inform the witness he is still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Turone, you can proceed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. ZIJAD SALIHAMIDZIC

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Salihamidzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So we can go on with my questions, I wanted to ask you, Mr. Salihamidzic, in the period you spent in Konjic after August '92 as operations officer and then as intelligence officer, did you become aware that the Celebici barracks was used as a detention facility for Serb prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you ever have a chance to visit this detention facility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not the prison, but in 1992, I did go there to collect some weapons. When Ljuta fell, I was the commander in Jablanica and I went there to take over a part of the armaments that were there at our disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you know at that time, that Celebici was already, at that time, a prison, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you ever get to know who was the commander of the Celebici detention facility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Could you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Pavo Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you know who was the deputy commander also?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Can you remember, approximately, when you learned that Mr. Pavo Mucic was the commander of the Celebici prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was around the end of August or, actually, in August, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you personally meet Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew him personally from before because the village where my wife comes from and just across the Neretva River is his place called Spiljani, and I know his brother who was there throughout the war, as well as the rest of his immediate family.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Mr. Salihamidzic, you testified about some contacts you had with Mr. Jerko Kostic. Do you know that Jerko Kostic was a member of an investigating commission entrusted with the task of interrogating and classifying the prisoners in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During my conversation with Mr. Jerko Kostic, and I knew him from before when he worked in the state security service in Mostar, I didn't get any information from him that he was involved in those activities because I told you yesterday what it was that he was dealing with. So I couldn't infer from the conversation what actually he was doing because he didn't ask me any questions in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I understand that you're saying that you didn't get any specific information about this commission and Jerko Kostic's work in it; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The subject, the two of us were discussing, I and Jerko Kostic, was not what you are now asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I understand that but my question was more general. Were you and are you aware that, in any case, Mr. Kostic was a member of that commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I had no occasion to learn that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Apart from the commission, et cetera, did Jerko Kostic ever tell you anything about the prison of Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have a great deal of confidence in people who used to work for the state security service, so that I couldn't come to any conclusions about what you're asking me, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you ever hear from any source any report or any information whatsoever about mistreatment of prisoners in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Reports in writing were not accessible to me in that time period, so I had no occasion to read any such reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I'm not talking about written reports. I'm talking about media reports and information whatsoever, you know, even TV, newspaper reports or any other information oral heard by you, not necessarily in writing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm a literate man. I do read the papers, and if something is written in the papers, everyone must have known about it. The papers carried such reports. Whether those reports are correct or not, I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Is that your testimony, that you read something about the possibility of mistreatment having taken place in Celebici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Such reports appeared in various newspapers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Delalic interviewed on television about reports and rumours of mistreatment in Celebici, some specific TV broadcasting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: More recently, you mean? When these trials began, this was shown on our television programme. I think this was done by an international organisation, and every month or every week, there would be a report about the trials going on here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: But my question was another one. Did you happen to see in 1991 Mr. Delalic interviewed on television about some reports -- 1992, I'm sorry, 1992, Mr. Delalic interviewed on television about reports and/or rumours of mistreatment in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't have occasion to see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right, thank you very much. Let's go now to the previous period when you were a commander of TO headquarters in Jablanica. I have just a few questions on that. You testified that you were appointed to that post by the ministry of defence upon a proposal of the Jablanica municipal assembly. Is this what you testified to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I have the assistance of the usher in showing the witness a document? We have copies for their Honours and for the Defence. There is the original Bosnian language and English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I ask you to wait just a few seconds and see this document. If you look at this document, my question is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I don't know if the witness has the documents already.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution document 245.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, is this the decision of the Jablanica municipal assembly proposing you as TO commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have seen this document. I don't notice the official stamp on it, on this document. Anyone could have written it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I understand that. This is how the document was provided to us by Ms. Residovic, I believe. In any case, my question is: Do you recognise it, because if you believe that this is not a correct document, just say that and I would not even tender it. If you say whether it has or not a stamp you recall and remember the document as such, please tell me whether you recognise it as such, otherwise just tell me what you think about this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will tell you. Mr. Sefer called me and we talked about whether I would accept to be as a senior officer with certain capabilities in the area of organisation and command and I accepted. The procedure that I insisted upon, because I'm very familiar with these procedures, was the one that was confirmed in the document that I offered to this honourable court. Whether Mr. Sefer in certain documents of relevance to himself took such a decision, I don't know, it is possible. But what is of relevance to me, as a senior officer, is the decision of my superior command and the document adopted by that command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I ask that this document be kept as marked for identification only for future needs?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, are you aware that the day after your appointment on 17 April, or is that true that the Jablanica municipality assembly nominated or proposed, for the same post of TO commander, another person, that is, Stipe Kopilas. Was my question clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very clear. That gentleman, Stipe Kopilas, could only be the chief of staff and not the commander, and that is what he officially was. He was my chief of staff because my staff was heterogeneous in composition, which means it consisted of Bosniaks, myself, my deputy, the chief of staff, the assistant for morality was Manigodic Zoran and so on. So that my command was heterogeneous or multi-ethnic in composition. My answer is in the affirmative. Stipe Kopilas was proposed as chief of staff and he was appointed through the same procedure as myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in May 1992, Jablanica had a crisis headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There is a regulation from the former period when crisis staffs existed in peace time. Then a special decision was taken later on, when the crisis staff ceased to exist, but instead, there were the war presidencies which functioned in those circumstances in which the assembly could not function. In my municipality, the assembly functioned and occasionally when it was unable to meet, the war presidency functioned as well. We had the good fortune for this to be possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I would like to show you another document, Mr. Salihamidzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to show this document to the witness? I have copies for their Honours and the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, take your time. You can look at this document and just tell me when you are ready to answer my question.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution document 246.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, you see that this document is dated 6 May, '92 and is published on the Jablanica official gazette. Would you agree with me that according to this document we should argue that the crisis headquarters existed and was in charge of organising the joint system of defence on the territory of the municipality? That's the point 1 in the decision you just read, a joint system of defence shall be organised in the Jablanica municipality area consisting of the Territorial Defence forces, the Croatian Defence Council, Green Berets, and all others, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object to this question, as the witness has already explained about the crisis staff and I also do not see the relevance of the question, in view of the contents of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour, since this document is not completely consistent of the possibility that now crisis headquarters existed in May, '92, I think I am entitled to ask the witness to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Is this matter in issue before us?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Well, it's a general issue of the power of war presidencies and crisis headquarters to issue military orders to deal with military matters, to deal with defence organisation, et cetera, so this is a relevant issue in the opinion of the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's a general principle, is it, that the war presidencies can issue as to military commands?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Not the general principle, Your Honour, I said general issue, which is relevant to the case because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: In respect of Jablanica municipality, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In respect to the authority of, war presidencies in general, of a crisis headquarters in general, in any municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: How does this portray that? How does this support that theory?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: One of the issues, of this case, is that some topics were regulated in a given sense by laws and worked in a different sense as a matter of fact. So this is one issue. But if Your Honour doesn't think that this is relevant, I withdraw any question about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't see the relevance of this, with this you're trying to bring out. It has nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: If Your Honour directs me to pass on, I will do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You must establish what you intend to say, this is what I am saying. And it is not, both in your own interest and the interest of the administration of justice in this trial, for you to pursue this type of argument. This does not disclose anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I will not press it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You're saying that the Jablanica municipality operates on behalf of the rest of the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I pass to another topic, Mr. Salihamidzic. You testified that about 50 soldiers from all of Jablanica were subordinated to TG-1 for Tinovo Brdo Operation when TG-1 was commanded by Polutak. My question is: Were any soldiers from the TO of Jablanica subordinated to TG-1 also later on when the commander was Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The composition of my military constricts was also heterogeneous. It is something I wish to tell their Honours. There were 50 combatants among whom there were both Serbs, Croats and Bosniaks. They participated at Tinovo Brdo and they subordinated themselves to the superior command of Tactical Group 1 of which Polutak was the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: All he asked you was whether, during the time that Ramic was commander of Tactical Group 1, were officers of Jablanica succoured to him too. This is what he's asking. Same as which what happened during the attack of Polutak. Did it also happen during the time of Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, he mentioned Tinovo Brdo and Mr. Polutak and not Delalic, so I am trying to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Sorry, maybe there was some misunderstanding in the translation because, actually, my question was exactly what Your Honour explained. I said we know you testified about 50 soldiers being subordinated to TG-1 or Mr. Polutak at that time. But what happened later on, were any soldiers from TO, Jablanica, subordinated to TG-1 also later on when the commander was Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness answered this question because he moved to Konjic. He answered to this in the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The story of the composition of his own units and that it was absolute features, that is what he was saying. But that has nothing to do with the answer, what is the exercise during Polutak's regime was also repeated when Delalic was commander. This is the question. You may have prepared answers which may not conform with questions and the question is what he's supposed to answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I answer that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Units from Jablanica, whose commander I was, and after that I went to Konjic, they did go there, but they were under the Tactical Group 2 in another area, in the direction of Tinovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So no soldier was subordinated to Tactical Group 1 at the time Delalic was the commander, is this your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Salihamidzic, when did you leave as TO commander of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: August, he said. August he said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I testified to that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Isn't that true that you were removed from your post of TO commander of Jablanica some time in June, '92, by Mato Sarlija also known as Daldza?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That information is wrong. I was only arrested, but not removed. Not removed, but arrested and then again put back to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I see. I come now to a more general question of the indictment, almost at the end. When you were questioned on cross-examination by Mr. Moran, you testified that a commander has the authority to issue orders to his subordinates and to punish them if the orders are not followed. Do you agree with me that if the commander is not present, the same power belongs to the deputy commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only if he is authorised by his superior to do this in writing, everything else would just be purely arbitrary decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And who takes care of the discipline if the commander is not present for a significant period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The one whom he authorises.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you mean that all the -- I withdraw it. You testified that in certain respects, and specifically intelligence, Mr. Delalic could give orders to the Konjic TO and you saw a document yesterday to this respect. This order from Mr. Delalic to the Konjic --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is not what the witness said. The witness was talking about an order and the directive from the supreme command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: This is what I understood yesterday, actually. Didn't you say that when you were talking about -- if there's a misunderstanding, just clarify please and I will take it. But didn't you say yesterday that in certain respects and specific intelligence, Mr. Delalic could give orders to the Konjic TO? Didn't you say that concerning the document signed by Delalic which was showed to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say that way, but we were obligated as intelligence department, either in Pasaric, Jablanica, to support the tactical group by intelligence. That is, to support tactical group which did not have its own command and was involved in a very important task of trying to leave decisions to Sarajevo. So we had obligation to provide him with intelligence in order to make that operation as successful as possible. Had the commander of the tactical group, have a developed intelligence unit, he could have, with our assistance, to more successfully resolve problems that we had. But he did not have any authority to issue orders to the municipal staffs, either to Jablanica or Konjic in terms of issuing orders. Only the units who arrived in this area were under his command and control and I said yesterday, as soon as the operation is finished, these units are returned to their original places and are again placed under the command of their own municipal staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right, thank you very much, Mr. Salihamidzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: This concludes my cross-examination, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any re-examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Salihamidzic, when asked by the Prosecutor whether you followed, whether Mr. Delalic was -- had given any statements, you said that you had been following this and that you had heard about it. Tell me, did you, during this trial, also read and hear about mistreatment of prisoners in Celebici? Was this in the same period of time that you read and heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What month are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question to you is based on your answer that you had been reading newspapers and that, and then when asked by the Prosecutor, you said that prisoners were mistreated at Celebici and then you said, when asked whether Mr. Delalic was doing that, that you said that's what you read. My question to you is, have you been reading this, during this trial, on this alleged mistreatment of prisoners in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When and in which newspaper did you learn about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not read about it here, no, not here, but in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During this trial, during the time period that covers this trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have an opportunity, I did read about it, but I cannot recall where. I read about the trials here and what these persons are accused of.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the only information about alleged mistreatment of prisoners in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall any newspaper where you may have read about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really cannot. I may have misspoken, but I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: -- cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I only want to ask, were any newspapers published in Konjic in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, during the entire war, they were not, only after the war. Just in order in not to misunderstand each other, we -- during the war, we did not have any opportunity to read newspapers. So it was after the war and that is what I talked about.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, we are very grateful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we have your next witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The next witness is Emin Zebic. Your Honours, just briefly as you suggested, you will recall General Divjak's testimony, he explained what regulations provided for the armed forces. It was MUP, TO and the HVO. During the presentation of evidence for the Defence, I will call two representatives of the MUP. This is a MUP representative from Jablanica and he can confirm certain facts that have already been presented here. And the other MUP representatives will be from Konjic and all this relates to the issue whether Zejnil Delalic at any point was commander of all armed forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: -- examined MUP representative from Konjic instead of going to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Examine MUP representative from Konjic, instead of going to --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, but I am not getting the interpretation through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Why not examine the representative of MUP from Konjic instead of examining a representative from the neighbouring municipality?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, both have been included in the witness list. The Prosecution claims that Zejnil Delalic was commander of all armed forces in the area, including Jablanica, Prozor, Hadzici and Konjic. And in the witness, Vasagic's (phoen) testimony, it came out, that this witness will be able to authenticate documents that are contained in the expert witness report. So this witness serves a dual purpose therefore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly swear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Will you please take your seats.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please introduce yourself by stating your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am Emin Zebic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, this is something that I keep repeating, but it is important. We speak the same language. In order for the court and everybody else present here to be able to follow our exchange, after I ask you a question, will you please listen to the sound coming out of the second headset and when you hear that out, please answer my question. Is that clear to you, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zebic, will you please tell the court when and where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born on 25 April 1945 in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what is your citizenship?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is your education and what are you by profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I graduated from a training college in political science and I am a teacher of physics and mathematics.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, where were you at the beginning of the war, in which town and what position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In early 1992, I was in Jablanica. I worked in the granite processing plant in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, at some time in 1992, join the defence forces in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As early as April, 1992, I joined the efforts to organise the defence of the Jablanica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, did you stay in this position or did you move on to other duties in the defence forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As early as 8 May, I moved to duty in the ministry of the interior and I was appointed commander of the public security station in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic who appointed you to the commander of the public security station in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pursuant to the law which was in effect then as it is today, commander of the public security station, including myself, was appointed by the minister of the interior of the republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, do you know who, at the time when you were appointed commander, was the Territorial Defence staff commander in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander of the TO staff in Jablanica at the time was Mr. Zijad Salihamidzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, do you know whether the Territorial Defence had any weapons at its disposal where it was and did you, at the public security station in Jablanica, have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic already spoken about it. The answer there in Konjic and the place (inaudible) and you only got about 20 per cent of the arms for which the municipal defence already paid for. You got evidence in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you whether the public security station had any weapons of its own.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The public security station did have its own weapons that belonged to it according to the organisational structure of the service.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Zebic, for how long did you hold the position of chief of the public security station in Jablanica in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Throughout 1992, I was chief of the public security station in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, in view of the position you held, were you a member of the war presidency of Jablanica municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in accordance with our regulations, I was also a member of the war presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was the war presidency superior to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The war presidency is a civilian body, but it was not superior to the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which was your superior body in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The public security station is a component part of the ministry of internal affairs of the republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, therefore, only the minister of the interior is superior to the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As chief of the public security station, Mr. Zebic, were you aware that the SDS of Konjic was arming a part of the Serb population and the members of the SDS of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we had such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What steps did you take in response to this information, Mr. Zebic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps I should inform their Honours that in the territory of Jablanica municipality, there was four per cent of the population were Serbs, that relations ever since before the second World War, which was strengthened during the second world war, were very good, that members of various ethnic groups respected one another and had good relations amongst themselves. And that even then, we wanted to preserve this mutual respect that we had for one another. That is why, in accordance with such a position, we called on the Serb population to surrender those weapons, to surrender them to us in the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was that done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After a conversation I personally had with representatives of the Serb people, the Serb inhabitants did surrender their weapons to the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of this testimony and the fact that this witness personally conducted these activities, I should like the witness to be shown Exhibit 144 annex D/4. Since this consists of a large number of documents, I should like to ask them to be marked for identification. I will tender them as a set and one number so that the witness may be able to recognise his signature and thus authenticate the documents which are already in evidence. I have enough copies for their Honours, the Prosecution and the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What is the document supposed to portray? What does it show?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The document confirms the submission of the Defence that the SDS was arming its members and also that the legal authorities tried by peaceful means to halt those illegal activities. Judge Jan remembered that, in the area of Jablanica, they did surrender their weapons and that they continued to live peacefully without any pressure from the legal authorities. This is in contradiction with the neighbouring municipality where they took up arms against the lawful authorities. It is not directly related, but since it supports a part of the testimony of the expert witness and is part of the supporting material of that testimony, you told us that we should authenticate those documents by the author of those documents, and the witness before us is one such author, so that this part of the documentation can be authenticated by a competent person. These are parts of the evidence. Obviously such evidence which is authenticated in this way, is important for the whole process of justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We have heard for so many minutes and so many words that the Jablanica group is more law abiding than the Konjic group where they did not surrender their weapons and had to be disloyal. That is what you're trying to say, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution is raising the question of legitimacy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: And all for which your client has been charged, that certain disloyalties in Konjic municipality resulted in certain things happening, that is what happened, not in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but one of the counts of the indictment is unlawful arrest and detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. Any unlawful arrest and detention in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. In any country -- Your Honours, I don't know whether we understand one another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: How can we when we have two different approaches to the issue? You can tender as many things as you like, if you think it is relevant, but I do not think it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The witness has been called because it was the suggestion of the Trial Chamber that these documents can only be authenticated by the author of those documents and that person is here before us, so I thought it would be useful for him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Counsel know what they should do when a witness who should tender the documents comes in. If it is only documents he has come to tender, you put the documents to him and he tenders them. We know how you tender documents. You tell him the original of it, how he has made them and don't tell us those stories about what happened in the whole situation. If documents is what you have called him to tender, then let him tender the documents or do they have to be relevant too. Not merely because you make a document, can you bring them in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You probably want to show that the conduct of the Serb population in Jablanica was different from what you encountered in Konjic. He has already given us testimony in regard to this situation, that they surrendered their weapons and they lived happily and their was no problem there. He can say that, being head of the security department.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We have heard evidence about the Ostrozac community where they were living and they are living happily even to today. We have heard evidence on that. These things do happen, not everybody behaves the same way. But when you come to defending events which have happened, the evidence the Trial Chamber requests is the event itself and what gave rise to the charges; although that's what the Prosecution should do, not necessarily the Defence, but you have your own way of defending so you can carry on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I can well understand your case is that these persons arrested from Bradina, Donje Selo, and there's another locality, they really rebelled against the state authority, but that's your case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just trying to show that where no one committed any offences and didn't rebel against the state, nothing happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You can ask him already and he can tell you. Why unnecessarily get involved in those documents? He's a support expert. He's speaking. He is head of the security and he knew what was happening in his municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, at the time, did you personally draw up an official report on the basis of which an agreement was reached on the peaceful surrender of weapons by the Serb population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I drew up an official report on that talk that we had.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you draw up that official report together with the representative of the Jablanica SDS, Mr. Zuza?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ranko Zuza was a representative of the Serb people in the area of Jablanica municipality and we did it together.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, did you personally sign every receipt on weapons surrendered by this population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did so personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hand over all those documents to the expert witness for the needs of his expert report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does each of those documents bear your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After that, did any person of Serb ethnicity get arrested in Jablanica municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No one was arrested because I said that we wanted to continue to nurture good relations with the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In spite of that, did Serb information media carry reports on arrests and torching of Serb villages in your area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were several such reports in the mass media in Serbia which spoke of the torching of Serb villages and the persecution of Serb inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Zebic, that it was Serbs and Mr. Zuza himself who handed over these documents denied such lies carried by these mass media?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course I know that, and I have a video to that effect and I have brought it with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, to confirm the credibility of this witness, we have not only the documents but also a short videotape showing Serbs from Ostrozac and Dobrigosce. And if you consider that we could view a minute or two of this tape, I would like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't consider it necessary. I think his testimony will be sufficient for the purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, in accordance with the law on the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did the MUP or, rather, the reserve force of MUP, are they also a component part of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was regulated by the law in force at the time. The police was a component part of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a minute, I don't understand. MUP has its own structure coming directly under the ministry of the interior. TO defence has its own structure coming directly under the ministry of defence. In a state of war, the MUP also comes under the ministry of defence or it still retains its independent connector? I hope you have understood what I've asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The MUP is under the ministry of the interior.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly so. The "MUP" is an abbreviation for the "Ministry of Internal Affairs".

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To make it clear to the court, please tell me, Mr. Zebic, whether in certain combat operations could MUP units be subordinated to the TO staff for that particular operation, being a component part of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The basis for this can be found in the law that I mentioned a moment ago, the law on defence. Therefore, units of the ministry of the interior could be transferred to the command of the Territorial Defence if the MUP, the ministry of the interior, gives such an order.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The remaining units of the ministry of the interior which were not subordinated in that way to the Territorial Defence for combat needs, under whose jurisdiction were they? To make it simpler, those who are not subordinated to the TO, who was their superior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those who are not transferred to other units, they remained within the jurisdiction of the public security station to which they belong.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, do you know Mr. Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, before we go on to that question, Your Honours, in view of the fact that the witness has -- viewing Exhibit D144 that he has before him, since he has confirmed that each document bears his signature, I should like to tender them into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: For the record, the Prosecution objects on grounds of relevancy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Maybe she wants to show the status of the detainees with regard to the role they played, and she wants to bring in these documents to show that those Serbs who cooperated with the authorities remained unharmed. That's probably what she wants to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the same authorities in Jablanica -- if the authorities were the same in Jablanica and Konjic, I would agree that there might be some relevance, but given what Ms. Residovic has said and what this witness has said, we don't believe it's relevant. In fact, you will note that the indictment doesn't contain any charges about events in Jablanica. We would also point out, just for the record, that the Prosecution has never stated that there were not some prisoners of war in Celebici. We have never stated that every person in Celebici was a civilian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is a slightly different position from what Mr. Niemann said. He said some of the detainees were prisoners of war and some were civilians. Now you're making the statement that they are all civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: She didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir. I said the opposite. We have never said that they were all civilians because that is not our position.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness has recognised his own documents and his signatures, and since the indictment says that Zejnil Delalic, according to the document dated 27th of July, was commander of all formations in that area too, I think this is a significant and a relevant document from the standpoint of the Defence. This is the classical way for a document to be authenticated, as far as I understand the procedure. The Prosecution is trying to establish certain details in their own way. I have tendered them. It is up to Your Honours to decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I have told you from the beginning, they are not relevant. Even for the purposes for which you are trying to tender them, they are not, because even if you want to show that a document spoke about Delalic being commander of all the forces, I don't see how this has any relevance to that type of declaration. What these documents are showing some internal arrangements in Jablanica were by peaceful means. Instructions were issued for persons to surrender their arms and they did, and they are documents to authenticate that, if I'm correct in interpreting what you say these documents are. That is all these documents are trying to show. How you think it supports charges against persons in Konjic community, if at all, I didn't see anywhere in the charges for not surrendering arms. There were people captured either because they were rebelling against the government and were taken to Celebici prison. This is what happened there, so I really didn't see the parallel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Let me try to make myself clearer. The Prosecution says that civilians and other persons were illegally detained. You have heard witnesses of the Prosecution and the Defence talking about attempts to negotiate with the population to surrender those illegal weapons and those negotiations produced no results and the town was attacked. In this way, we are showing that the legal authorities did everything and that the arrest and detention of persons was a legitimate act. This is one of the counts of the indictment against not only my client but also the others. However, I have heard you, Your Honour, and, of course, it is within your discretion. According to rule 89, you can reject the evidence that I am tendering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If it is irrelevant. I cannot reject evidence which is relevant. It would not even be proper to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have tried to the best of my ability to explain why the Defence considers it is relevant, so I appeal to you to make your ruling. I cannot say more than to say that these documents confirm the legitimate arrest and detention of persons anywhere in Jablanica or in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed with other questions, if you have any.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, the persons that you took over the weapons from, peacefully, what part of Jablanica did they live in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those persons lived in a settlement called Ostrozac which is about 10 kilometres from Jablanica, in the direction of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the negotiations with representatives of the Serb people from this area, did you know that Zejnil Delalic too, as a neighbour of theirs, had talked to these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, while talking to them and also talking to my associates, because in the police, I had people of Serb ethnicity and others too living in Ostrozac. And we learned that Mr. Zejnil Delalic was also urging that disagreements be overcome by peaceful means, including this problem of the illegal possession of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Though the court has learned about this fact from some Prosecution and Defence witnesses, I should just like to ask you whether you know where Zejnil Delalic was born and grew up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course I know. I met Zejnil Delalic while he was still a young man. I worked in Ostrozac as a teacher of physics and mathematics, and I even taught some members of his family, so I know he was born in Ostrozac.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me now, Mr. Zebic, do you know that Zejnil Delalic -- maybe you can tell us when you learned about this. Do you know whether Zejnil Delalic became a military commander of some sort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to my knowledge, he became a military commander, I think, somewhere around the beginning of August 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what is the position he acquired then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to military doctrine, this is known as a Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, were you aware of the task of that Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't know the precise task, except globally, that it involved attempts to deblock Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me please, Mr. Zebic, as you too are a component part of the armed forces pursuant to the law on the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did Zejnil Delalic, as commander of Tactical Group 1, at any point in time in '92, was he a superior or a superior commander to you or any of your units in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I was explaining a moment ago that the only command authority is the ministry of the interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina or, rather, the minister of the interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina was the only one who could give orders to public security stations or police units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, as you were saying that sometimes certain units could be resubordinated to TO staffs, in 1992, did any one of your police units come under the command of one of the commanders of the Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of our smaller units but within the units of the municipal staff, with the permission or, rather, following the orders of the ministry of the interior, were transferred to the Tactical Group whose task was to lift the blockade of Sarajevo in the area of Trnovo and also in the operation to liberate Tinovo Brdo, as it was called.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The remaining MUP units or the Jablanica police station which did not participate in these two operations, under whose jurisdiction were they; that was, who was their commander or body in command of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The remaining units were under my command as I was the chief of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think we can stop now and reassemble at noon.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, do you remember that a moment ago you answered my question that certain units of MUP, which were subordinate to municipal staff, were engaged in fighting at Tinovo Brdo in the area towards Trnovo, do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, if you can remember, to whom were these units subordinate in the first case, that is at Tinovo Brdo, and to whom were they subordinate when they went to Trnovo in order to lift the siege, and also if you can recall when this was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the first case, the units, as far as I can recall, were subordinate to Mr. Mustafa Polutak. And in the second case, I think that the commanders were Neletovic (phoen) and Alic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, as a chief of the public security station, you may know this, was there a prison in Jablanica in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, in 1992, there was no prison in Jablanica, and as far as I know, it had not existed before that and it has not existed since.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether in 1992, in -- was there a court or a public Prosecutor's office in Jablanica in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no court and there was no public Prosecutor's office there in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Jablanica have possibilities set forth, by law, to set up a court or a public Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The organisation of the public Prosecutor's office and court, according to the law of that period, was not in the competence of municipal authorities, so that Jablanica municipality could not do it on its own.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This court has heard enough evidence regarding the blockade and influx of refugees, but I am going to ask you two pointed questions: Did a certain amount of refugees also arrive in Jablanica during 1992, and if they did, where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I witnessed a large number of refugees coming to Jablanica in the early part of 1992. Many of them arrived in Jablanica planning to stay there, but when Jablanica filled up, they continued on, westward, towards Croatia. That is when all the accommodation that we had available, first, of course, the hotel accommodations and then of school buildings, when all of these was filled up, then the overflow of refugees started moving westward.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, what were the living conditions of all of the people who lived in your area? Did you have enough supplies for regular, normal living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jablanica is a small town, under 13,000 population and does not have great resources. And does not have its own food production facilities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you going to add something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I also wanted to add that we were cut off from the south and we couldn't go to Sarajevo. You could go to central Bosnia, so the food supplies, the food stocks that we had in warehouses and privately, it was all that was available and this coincided with the large influx of refugees. So the living conditions were very, very poor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, let's move on to another area. Mr. Zebic, do you know where Celebici is located and do you know whether there was a barracks there? If you know, that is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do know where Celebici is, it is a small town on the main M-17 Highway between Jablanica and Konjic, about 15 kilometres from Jablanica and about 10 kilometres from Konjic. I know that from before the war, that there were some military facilities there. It is something that you can actually see from the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find out at some point that there was a prison there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had heard about it, but only later.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally ever visit the prison in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never visited it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, you started to say that you used to -- that you knew Mr. Zejnil Delalic and his family. Can you tell me whether, during 1992, you met Mr. Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I said that I knew him from much earlier. I even knew his parents. Later on I learned that he became a respected business person. And I also learned that, in 1992, he came back to Bosnia-Herzegovina and I even met him, sometime in early June.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What were the circumstances under which you met him in June, and what was he engaged in at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you a moment ago what the general situation was in the area where we lived. There was a lack of all kinds of food and other goods. I had personally heard that Mr. Delalic was in a position to help provide certain supplies. And so, we turned to him to try to help us find some equipment that we needed for the police force.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Apart from that time, did you ever meet Mr. Zejnil Delalic during 1992, either in Jablanica or in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic became personally engaged in trying to reopen the railroad aligned between Pasaric and Jablanica. That was the only section of the railroad which was open to traffic. So I saw him with the railroad people there at that time because he was personally, as I said, involved in it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, I have another area in which I believe you may assist the Trial Chamber in this matter. As a person who was working in the public security station, can you tell us where the files are kept on persons who have criminal records?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to our regulations, the courts, after the sentence comes into force, will send the files to the place of residence of the person who had been convicted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic, did you at any time, on anyone's request in 1996, verified information on the criminal record of Mr. Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me state that, I have stated this before, I am not objecting to the question, and I am not exactly sure the point Ms. Residovic is wanting to get at. But if she wishes to bring in evidence of, in effect, the good reputation of Mr. Delalic, we will be bringing in, and we certainly will have the right to bring in, contrary evidence in rebuttal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the expert report, there was a document and I just wanted to find out whether this document was compiled with the knowledge of the witness here. And I am not trying to bring up what Ms. McHenry is suggesting, so it is just to authenticate or corroborate a document from the witness -- the expert witness report. And this also would be my last question of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You can ask questions without putting his reputation in issue, that's nothing. If your question does not put his reputation in issue, it should be welcome. But if you do, then the Prosecution will be entitled to suggest something to the contrary later.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am just trying to present the facts that concern this indictment, his personal life and reputation is not a matter for this proceedings. But since this document came in, I just wanted the make sure whether he verified the authenticity of this document. But I don't know whether -- I had just wanted to confirm the authenticity of everything, of all the documents that the expert witness submitted in his report. And I think that this witness has confirmed that, therefore, I have no further questions of this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think it's okay. Any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I have a few questions I would like to ask you, but before I start asking you some question, if you don't understand me, please indicate that you don't understand me and I'll try to rephrase my question, okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And I am going to be asking you also a series of questions that require simply a yes or a no answer, so I would ask that you restrict yourself to a yes or no answer if you can, is that all right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will try.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During the course of your direct examination, you talked about the situation in Jablanica and I would like to talk a little bit about that as well, okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war began, was there a court and Prosecutor in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me what responsibilities there were during peacetime of the local authorities in Jablanica with respect to prisons and prisoners?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There was no prison in Jablanica, he said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I am just laying a little bit of foundation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: How can they have responsibilities there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I have a hypothetical question here, let's assume that that the situation in Jablanica was such that there was not the peaceful transfer of weapons and the people did not give themselves up peacefully, okay, that is the Serb population. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Your hypothetical example is still not complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Right, Your Honour, I just want the make sure he understood what I have said thus far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He's the head of security, he must understand what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Where would you put 150 to 200 people, if you needed to, that were detained in a hypothetical situation, where you needed to have them in the time of war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It really is a hypothetical question and the question can be a corresponding one. It would be in a similar situation or a similar facility as those in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And in that kind of a situation, there would be an organisation, would there not, that would be responsible for that prison, is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you're asking me with respect to Jablanica, that prison was not in Jablanica and we would have no authority there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that. My question is a hypothetical one, which deals with what if the same kind of a situation existed in Jablanica? There would be an organisation, would there not, that would be in charge or responsible for the prison, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there at any time after 1992, a prison in Jablanica that existed, that held either military personnel or civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was no prison whatsoever in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So are you telling me, sir, as head of security if there were 150 to 200 people in Jablanica that needed to be detained in a facility, that you wouldn't know what organisation would be responsible for that facility, is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions, thank Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any further questions? Because I didn't see you carry any papers at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's because it's going to be so short I don't need notes. May it please the court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: My name is Tom Moran and I represent a man name Hazim Delic, he's the last man over there, you don't know Hazim, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: We heard the term public security station, used not just by you, but by a lot of witnesses and the I just wanted to make it clear that what the public security station is, is the police station. It's where the police who would investigate, what I will refer to as normal crimes, everything from drunk driving to burglary to theft, that's who works out of the public security station, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can hear the translation behind me still going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And one last question, sir, and then I think I'll be done with you. You, of course -- actually two last questions. You, of course, negotiated with the Serbs in your municipality and they voluntarily surrendered their weapons. Now, what I want to ask you is, did you have a contingency plan to arrest them if they did not voluntarily surrender their weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not have any contingency plans, we simply went to these discussions in the hope of getting a positive resolution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: And, by the way, the laws involving illegal possession of weapons, they were enforced no matter what the ethnic background of the person with the weapon, isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you, very much. Your Honour, I pass the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let me ask a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What would you have done if negotiations broke down to surrender the weapons if you did not agree to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We probably would have undertaken some other steps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What type of steps would you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a police tactics, there are also searches as a method, searches of houses, properties, backyards, things like that. And if during the searches some weapons were to be found, the owners of weapons found there would be duly prosecuted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: The defence of Esad Landzo has no questions of this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you, any examination? The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, my name is Theresa McHenry and I am a member of the Prosecution team. I think as trial counsel has said, if you don't understand a question, please just ask me to rephrase it. And a number of questions that I am going to ask, I believe, will only require a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, I believe that I understood you, that MUP units could be subordinated to military units on those occasions when MUP so authorised, is that correct? Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, for any subordination of units that belong to public security stations, the approval of the ministry of the interior was required.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And, sir, did the ministry of interior, in Sarajevo, have to authorise that or could you as head of the MUP in Jablanica, could you do it yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Without the approval of the ministry of the interior, this could not be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I understand that. My question is: You were the head of the ministry of interior in Jablanica and then your superiors were in Sarajevo. My question is: Could you authorise certain MUP units under your control to be subordinated to military or did the authorisation have to come from MUP in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ministry of the interior in Sarajevo, as we said a moment ago, is a part of the defence forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. When units are transferred, then it is the ministry that had to give approval for these units to be sent to join other formations.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: The ministry in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: In those cases where MUP units were subordinated to military units, those units would then be under the ultimate authority of the main staff of the armed forces for Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This is what he said in his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. I'm going to ask a follow-up question. I want to make sure I understood the foundation. If he just says "yes," then I will move on to my follow-up questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question more clearly?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, in those cases where MUP units would be subordinated to military units, the MUP units, the subordinated ones, would then fall under the authority of the main staff of the armed forces for Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're asking me questions about the military organisation. Those units are subordinated to the commander of the unit they are joining. And further on from there regarding the chain of command, that is regulated by military rules and regulations.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Fair enough. Do I understand you that you're not familiar with the military rules and regulations that would regulate the chain of command above; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I am not familiar and I don't have to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Fair enough, sir, thank you. Am I correct that those units that had not been subordinated to military units, those units would not be under the authority of the main staff of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This is, again, what he said in his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: If so, then all he has to do is confirm it and I can go on to my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You mean you are repeating what was said in his evidence in chief as part of your examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I believe that this logically follows from what he stated. I don't believe he stated it explicitly, and so that there can be no question that somehow I've made a jump that, to me, seems logical, I thought it would be most fair and most efficient just to clarify that and I will then go on to my next question. Obviously, if he has stated it already, he can so state and then I'll move on to my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If he stated it already, he should state it again for you to be satisfied?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: He hasn't stated it in those words. I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: In your own words, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, I don't think he has specifically addressed this position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Ask the next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: MUP units that had not been subordinated to a military unit, were those units considered a component part of the armed forces or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The units that were not transferred to others remained within the jurisdiction of the ministry and their commander is the commander of that unit. In my particular case, I was in command of the units that remained in my public security station, and I'm accountable to the minister of the interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: What I'm just trying to clarify, sir, just to see if you can help me understand it because I don't, I thought you stated that the minister of interior, that that ministry was a component part of the armed forces; did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're asking me something that is stated in our regulations. I'm just telling you about the segment related to the ministry of the interior. From there on, these things are regulated by the regulations of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, if I understood you correctly, sir, the ministry of interior is a component part of the armed forces of Bosnia according to the regulations; is that correct? Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And was the answer "yes"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Does that, to your understanding, mean that all MUP units, including you, were considered a component part of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina also? If you don't know, you can say you don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, am I correct that in May of 1992 there was a crisis staff in Jablanica or crisis headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A crisis staff is a leftover from the former system and possibly it existed until regulations were passed on the new organisation. Those regulations were passed, if I remember correctly, around the 20th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, have you ever seen any editions of the official gazette of the Jablanica municipality crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Any editions?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Any editions, publications of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Have you seen the official gazette of the municipality of Jablanica? This is the question because in the script it said "any additions," and I was wondering what is addition.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what exactly you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Can I ask that the witness just be shown Prosecution Exhibit 246.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What do you intend to ask about this gazette?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, among other things, I intend to ask just a very few questions about the municipality crisis staff and orders that may have come out of it regarding the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I find it difficult to see the relevance of it. I find it fairly difficult.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it will just take a couple of minutes but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It doesn't matter even if it doesn't take any time if it's irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I agree with you, Your Honour.
