The reason, as I understand it, that Ms. Residovic showed the witness a document about this witness's appointment and had it admitted into evidence is because she stated it showed that the regulations were all being carried out in full in Jablanica. I certainly believe -- and I believe that there was some testimony about this from the Defence expert witness. So certainly I believe I am entitled to ask a few questions about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What are you challenging in the regularity of his appointment?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'm not challenging anything about the regularity of his appointment. What I am challenging is the proposition that in Jablanica everything worked strictly according to the regulations, as opposed to because of the difficult circumstances there were some things that were dealt with in other ways. This witness, as a member of that group, can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Why don't you ask about those questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Let me ask that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object. I did not show this witness any document about his appointment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Let me just ask the question directly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, were you a member of the Jablanica crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not a member of the crisis staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Having seen the document, in your role as head of the police, did you ever see the official gazettes of the Jablanica crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Is what you have before you a copy of, at least, portions of the gazette of the Jablanica crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Was there a time, sir, when sometime in 1992 the crisis staff took any actions regarding the dismissal or request for dismissal of the head of the MUP, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You mean in regards to him? He was the head of the MUP there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes. I don't believe he was head of it for all of 1992, so I wanted my question to be slightly broader.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware whether or not any time in 1992 the crisis staff took any action dismissing or seeking the dismissal of the head of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never attended meetings of the crisis staff so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, you stated that you were aware in 1992 of reports in the Serb media about events in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Are you finished with the gazettes and the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, I am finished with the gazettes. I have no further questions and I'm moving to another area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can proceed. Repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, you stated that in 1992 you were aware of reports in the Serb media about events alleged to have taken place in Jablanica; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: How did you become aware of those reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could be heard on the radio and on television.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Did you also at the time hear any reports about the Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at the time. I heard nothing about the Celebici camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, to your knowledge, during the time that Mr. Delalic was commander of Tactical Group 1, were any MUP units ever subordinated to Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Jablanica, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated in direct that you supplied to the expert witness certain public security documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Receipts.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: -- receipts. Did you also supply to the expert witness or to anyone in the Defence any orders from Sarajevo dealing with the subordination of MUP units to any Tactical Groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The documents I handed over are receipts which I personally signed for the weapons taken over.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Let me just ask: Are you aware if documents exist from Sarajevo authorising the subordination of any MUP units to any Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please clarify your question a little? What documents are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'm asking, sir, have you ever seen any documents from the ministry of interior in Sarajevo authorising the subordination of any MUP units in Jablanica to any Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen any such documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, do you know anything about who was responsible for Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, will you please help me to get to the truth? You are asking me something that I have already answered saying I didn't know because I was never there. And about the events and the status of those facilities, I learned much later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This witness doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, am I correct that you don't know anything about what happened --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He has said he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: This is a different question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Still following on about Celebici?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'm just clarifying that he knows nothing whatsoever about the Celebici camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This is what he says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This is what he has just said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: If it's clear that he knows nothing about Celebici whatsoever, I will go on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, am I correct that at some point recently you were informed that the Prosecution had requested the opportunity to speak with you before you testified?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Did anyone ever inform you that the Prosecution had asked if they might speak with you before you gave your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: No further questions. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any re-examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No re-examination, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think this is all the Trial Chamber wants of you. You are discharged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: May we have your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, obviously we didn't plan our time very well and we asked that the next witness be brought here at 2.00 to be ready to testify. I beg your indulgence because we didn't expect the cross-examination to be over so soon. He will be at our disposal at half past two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The credit goes to Ms. McHenry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Okay. I think we need not waste our time now. We shall rise and reassemble at 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.52 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, kindly advise your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I call witness Hamza Ajanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What is he going to depose about?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, you can see that I am trying to reduce the number of questions to only the most relevant facts in order to speed things up. This witness has certain knowledge of facts which have already been presented and in the strictest sense of the word, it may be doubtful whether he should testify at all. It is your decision, really, if we should have this witness' testimony presented today. Tomorrow I have another witness that I intend to call. This witness will talk to the role of coordinator and the Operation Oganj. As well as his knowledge of certain commanders in the Konjic area and whether they were involved in the Tactical Group 1 or not. I know that some of this information may be redundant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You're not sure, why examine him? It's just duplication.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I will not insist, but I have to tell you that I do not have another witness for today. I will have the next witness coming in tomorrow. Because these are the witnesses which have been called before our status conference, that is, they were called last week and this is why I have invited this witness into the courtroom today. I know that he can corroborate the facts that may have been established by now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually, you can see the wisdom of coordination about witnesses which you should call. Is it not necessarily because we want to be faster here, it's the expense of bringing him itself. It's unreasonable if his evidence will not improve what we are doing here. We really do not need this witness because whatever he would say, from a short summary of what you indicated, has been said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honours. This witness would only confirm the already established facts. However, since this witness has been called much earlier, so he just happened to be here and I agree with you this witness need not be called today, but I do not have another witness for you right now. Maybe I can make a call through and have -- try to arrange that the next witness be called maybe after 4.00 today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Why unnecessarily burden the record? Just because he's here is no reason that he must be examined. Maybe 4.00 then we meet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That's a long time. Three thirty?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: 4.00, Your Honours, because we need to contact the witness. He needs to prepare. I have talked to the victim and witnesses unit in the morning. I think that they would need time to make arrangements so that the witness would be ready to be here at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think we can afford to wait instead of repeating what has been done, which is of no value at all to put yourself on the Trial Chamber. And I suppose you would like to rest your voice, too. Yes, we'll have to adjourn until 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. My apologies to you, Mr. Ajanovic, for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Are you interested in this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, since we don't know what he's going to say, we don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You mean you couldn't indicate what he's going to say from the short summary?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, we don't get the short summary, that's something that only the Trial Chamber gets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much for wasting your time. I wish I could have saved you that trouble. We'll rise and come back at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has been informed that you have not succeeded in tracing your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Together with representatives of the victims and witnesses unit, we went to the hotel immediately but the witness was not planned for today. And with a unit assistant, they went somewhere and we waited for them until ten to four. As they did not appear by then, we really don't know which part of town they are in, so I was unable to call the witness to appear in court this afternoon. I apologise. I thought that the witness was in the hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: One would have thought that these witnesses are personally under a certain amount of protection who think or know that they are always at hand to be contacted by you, so that if need be they might be the next ones to be called for evidence. I thought that was the position.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do not know what is the procedure and the rules of the victims and witnesses unit. They probably have some kind of procedure. When a witness is free, they probably take him somewhere to show him something, but the victims and witnesses unit tried their best to trace them, but I'm afraid I have no control over the procedure of that unit and I had assumed that they were at the hotel. Otherwise, I wouldn't have suggested that I go and fetch him immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Have you any other witness for today?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is the last witness we have for this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: For this whole week?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This a surprise to me because you have a long list of witnesses. Already within two days your witnesses for the week have been disposed of? Because we started only yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to the way the examination progressed, we thought that five witnesses was sufficient for one week. But following your instructions, I reduced the scope of the examination and I think that the Prosecution did the same so that the testimony evolved far more efficiently. I had expected today's witness to be finished by the end of the day so that the next witness could come tomorrow. Also, according to the victims and witness unit, they bring in witnesses only at the end of the week for the following week, so this is probably in order to keep the costs of the Tribunal down. So that as we were not quite prepared and didn't know how this procedure would affect our planning, that is what happened. Because if you recall in the first week, we went through three witnesses only and there were witnesses waiting for a fortnight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: There is one witness so you could not have finished your witnesses for the week. It means there's still an outstanding witness who we haven't called.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: So you still have a witness tomorrow, providing his evidence is relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Which is some indication of what we have been hearing. Because you have a list for next week which appears to follow your usual pattern of saying the same things for any of them. In any event, you still have a witness we haven't seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: So you could not have exhausted your witnesses for the week.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. We will hear that witness tomorrow. His name is Sadik Dzuhmur. We had planned him according to our schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't know. He was one of those who perhaps falls in line with your normal way of tendering evidence. Still, you put him down as giving evidence about defence structures and on command responsibilities. This is what you have him down for.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I explained this morning when witness Emin Zebic was here, I said that we would be calling a representative of MUP Konjic and a representative of MUP Jablanica because they have to do with defence structures. This witness was a member of MUP Konjic and deputy commander of the public security station at Konjic and we believe that he is a relevant witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Are we now sure that we can have him tomorrow because we have been told that you expected him this afternoon and we couldn't have him. So how will we be sure he will be here tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are absolutely sure, Your Honour, because the witness was not told about this afternoon as we hadn't known what would happen with Witness Ajanovic, and that is why he didn't expect us to call him. In the morning, he will certainly appear in this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's a frustrating experience to wait for witnesses when, in fact, we should be quite busy. I don't know. Now, it is important for us to know exactly the witnesses we will be having next week so that -- as I said, I have it but I say I'm not too sure whether they will all be here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, among those witnesses is General Polutak who was the first commander of Tactical Group 1. Then there is brigadier Dzambasevic who was the first member of the TO staff of Bosnia-Herzegovina who came to Konjic, and at the same time, he was in charge of the Operation JUG. Then there's Dzelilovic Mustafa, the only person coming from the municipality of Hadzici and who could testify in a similar way as other witnesses about the possible responsibility of Mr. Delalic for all formations of the armed forces. Then there is Salih Hruvic, TO commander for Prozor. Then we have another commander later on the list, but if this one provides all the relevant information for the court, we will not be calling this second representative from Prozor because he is to testify about the same circumstances, that is, all the formations of the armed forces within the territory of Prozor municipality. Then there is Saban Duracic who may testify about certain activities and responsibilities of the joint command, the Operation Oganj, the visit of journalists to the combat areas. He may refer to some other evidence that has been admitted by the Trial Chamber in the course of the Prosecution case. So that I think these are important and relevant witnesses from the standpoint of the Defence, and I think that you will, for the first time, have the opportunity to hear persons who were directly involved in the command of Tactical Groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: All these are testimonies in support of command authority and exercise of command authority?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They are all linked to command authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: In addition to what has been said before now?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but now these are persons whom may explain the link between the command responsibility of the commander of Tactical Group 1 and the commands at other levels, and especially the command of prisons, because we will have the commander who was the commander prior to Mr. Delalic of Tactical Group 1; then another commander responsible for the battles around Sarajevo and who is familiar with the responsibilities of commanders and any possible link between their responsibility and control over prisons. So we are not talking any longer about the responsibility of coordinators but, rather, the responsibility of commanders on the basis of their own knowledge and experience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose then we will meet tomorrow morning at ten a.m. and we will continue our proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will now rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 27th day of May, 1998 at 10.00 a.m. 23 24 25
